name: Mawa Bati
instructions: 1. Mix khoya and maida to form a smooth dough, ensuring no lumps remain.
2. Create a stuffing by mixing finely chopped dry fruits, a pinch of cardamom, and a little khoya.
3. Divide the dough into equal portions, flatten them, place the stuffing in the center, and roll into smooth balls.
4. Heat ghee in a deep pan and fry the balls on low-medium heat until they turn deep golden brown.
5. Prepare a sugar syrup (one-string consistency) infused with saffron and rose water.
6. Drop the fried bati into the warm syrup and let them soak for at least 2 hours before serving.
description: Mawa Bati is a larger, more opulent version of the classic Gulab Jamun, famously hailing from the state of Madhya Pradesh. It is a quintessential festive treat, often served at weddings and celebrations, cherished for its dense, melt-in-the-mouth texture and the royal crunch of dry fruits hidden inside.
